evidence: Receiving DO2 never below ~8.2 mg/L (24-28h dip) vs 2.0 mg/L minimum; recovers to ~11-12.4 mg/L after routine air step at 28h
Receiving P assay at 48h = 3.48 g/L vs source batches 2.98/3.02/3.06 g/L; 36h assay 1.27 vs 1.02-1.12 g/L - on or ahead of healthy source
Transfer multiplier ~0.989 indicates near-identical source/receiving behavior
Forward model KEEP: 576 kg, feasible in 5/5 sensitivity members, min DO 7.85 mg/L post-decision
Forward model COMBINED nominal 595 kg, but sensitivity non-overlap is small and model is source-calibrated, not the hidden receiving realization
args.rationale: Receiving batch is a normal case: DO2 stays 8-14.6 mg/L (minimum ~8.2, well above the 2.0 mg/L constraint) and product concentration at 48h (3.48 g/L) matches or exceeds all three healthy source batches (~3.0 g/L) with the same batch-phase pattern including the standard 24-28h oxygen dip and recovery after the routine air increase at 28h. No oxygen-constraint violation, no stall, no deficit. Although the nominal source-calibrated forward model shows a modest gain for COMBINED (595 kg vs 576 kg), that model is not the hidden receiving realization and a 20% feed cut plus aeration change would deviate from a trajectory that historically completes at ~7 g/L without intervention, with risk of reduced mass accumulation and unmodeled receiving-process differences. KEEP retains full product mass and satisfies the oxygen constraint with large margin.
args.uncertainty: Moderate: the ~3% nominal model advantage for combined interventions is within the model's calibration error relative to the hidden receiving realization; DO2 forecasts keep min ~6.7-8.9 mg/L (sensitivity range) under KEEP, so oxygen feasibility is robust. The main risk of KEEP is forfeiting a small modeled yield gain; the main risk of acting is slowing a healthy, slightly-ahead-of-source fermentation. Assay values are 4h delayed, so current state could be slightly ahead of the last P assay (positive direction).
